summary: Preserved PR 3235's valid exact-request Qwen image preprocessing optimization, but independently reproduced PR 3277's four counterexamples. The candidate does not implement prompt-independent explicit save/load, cross-worker or restart persistence, or Qwen video/audio caching; no speculative architecture change is claimed without Qwen-VL weights.

tests.what_was_measured: The exact candidate's trusted-ID hit, single-flight cold miss, key scoping, bypass, and defensive-copy regression coverage; 4 tests passed.
Same content ID with changed prompt produced unequal keys and two preprocessing calls; a fresh processor recomputed once; video and audio cache keys were None.
Focused cache, identity, parser, and OpenAI protocol compatibility; 115 tests and 30 subtests passed.
Modified Qwen processor source compiled successfully.

remaining_limitations: The rendered prompt remains part of the Qwen request preprocessing cache key, so the same image ID is reprocessed for a changed prompt.
The OpenAI-compatible API has no explicit preprocessing save operation and later caller-selected load operation.
Cache ownership remains local to each processor/tokenizer-worker process and entries do not survive restart.
Qwen video and audio requests bypass this cache path.

An AMD Instinct MI350X gfx950 was visible, but GPU execution was not used: no qualifying Qwen-VL model weights were available, and the tiny Llama fixture cannot validate Qwen preprocessing or cache semantics.
Qwen-VL end-to-end correctness, semantic equivalence, and performance were not validated because model weights were unavailable.
